name: Deposits, readiness, penalties
desc: Standardize study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects.

letters.desc: AEMA supports standardized readiness criteria such as deposits and site control for the FLFT, consistent with generator interconnection but appropriately scaled for large loads, to deter speculative projects while enabling the cost-allocation benefits of the flexible track.
quotes: AEMA believes the FLFT provides a crucial, market-based choice for large loads: (1) interconnect as an inflexible load and potentially bear the costs for the resulting, often slow and expensive, network upgrades; or (2) interconnect as a flexible load via the FLFT, avoid triggering those upgrades, and get online faster at lower cost. This protects all other ratepayers from socializing upgrade costs.

letters.desc: The filing backs heightened financial deposits and non-financial readiness indicators such as site control and permitting progress to filter out speculative queue entries. It warns against a pure pay-to-play deposit model that well-capitalized applicants could game by holding multiple queue slots.
quotes: Increasing the requirements on interconnecting large load customers is critical to ensure that utilities and system operators are not planning and preparing for load that will not ultimately show up, and that load is committing to pay the cost of preparing the system. Without this discipline, other new large loads will suffer the consequences of an interconnection process bogged down by speculative projects, and all ratepayers risk being left paying the cost of preparing the system for new load that never materializes.

As with the generator interconnection process, it is critical to ensure compatibility with commercial realities and to adopt a mix of financial and non-financial readiness requirements to accommodate a range of business models and avoid a 'pay to play' model whereby well-capitalized large loads may be able to buy their way into multiple queue positions.

letters.desc: AES asks FERC to issue a policy statement clarifying how termination fees paid under construction service agreements for transmission network upgrades should be reflected in transmission rates, providing market certainty without restructuring the existing cost-assignment model.
quotes: AES believes that the Commission could provide certainty to the market by issuing guidance, whether in the form of a policy statement or otherwise, regarding how termination fees from construction service agreements associated with transmission network upgrades should be accounted for in transmission rates.

letters.desc: Alliant Energy supports study deposit requirements for large load interconnections, noting no such framework exists today in MISO. It endorses Order No. 2023's generator deposit structure as a starting point but calls for flexibility so transmission providers can tailor deposit sizes to load characteristics rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all rule.
quotes: Alliant Energy supports implementing study deposits requirements for large load interconnection studies, as no such framework currently exists in MISO.

a one-size-fits-all approach would be counterproductive.  Large load interconnection processes vary across transmission providers, and imposing uniform requirements risks disrupting effective practices already in place.

letters.desc: Amazon Energy endorses applying generator-style standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to large loads. It argues these measures deter non-viable and speculative requests and reduce cascading restudies.
quotes: Amazon Energy supports the proposal in the ANOPR that, "like generating facilities, load and hybrid facilities should be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties,"

requiring large load interconnection customers to make upfront study deposits, demonstrate a degree of project readiness (e.g., site control or an executed facilities construction contract), and face withdrawal penalties if they exit after certain milestones will discourage non-viable or speculative large load requests.

letters.desc: ACORE supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for load and hybrid facilities to give greater certainty that interconnection requests will materialize.
quotes: to subject load and hybrid facilities to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to provide greater certainty on the likelihood that such interconnection requests will materialize.

letters.desc: ATC supports LGIP-style deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for loads meeting the threshold, arguing these tools focus study resources on committed customers. ATC asks the Commission not to duplicate existing local safeguards such as ATC's Project Commitment Agreement.
quotes: ATC generally supports subjecting loads that meet the threshold applicability requirements to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties, analogous to the LGIP.  Eliminating speculative requests for significant load growth from consideration by implementing these stringent requirements would help focus time, costs, and resources to expeditiously interconnect serious customers.

ATC respectfully requests that the Commission refrain from disturbing existing processes already in place to address the risk of speculative load and consider the risk of duplicating existing processes that could result in unintended consequences.

letters.org: Americans for a Clean Energy Grid
letters.desc: ACEG supports requiring financial commitments from large loads seeking interconnection to weed out speculative projects and ensure regional plans reflect real demand. Loads that are incorporated into regional transmission plans should pay their fair share over the life of the asset.
quotes: a requirement that large loads (50 MW or larger, for instance) are backed by stringent financial commitments and are reported to regional transmission planners so that significant loads can be adequately supported and integrated into the larger grid.

Large loads that are incorporated into forecasts used to plan and develop new infrastructure should pay their fair share over the life of the asset; planning processes should ensure that such forecasts only incorporate loads that are not speculative or temporary.

Should the Commission revert to a strict direct-assignment funding mechanism for load interconnection-related network upgrades, it risks stymying the very development it seeks to accelerate, as this will only harm transmission developers' ability to attract capital and make needed investments that benefit all transmission users.

letters.desc: Arevia backs standardized deposits as effective deterrents against speculation but proposes exempting projects with binding contracts and site control.
quotes: Arevia would support standardized study deposits.
Arevia believes that deposits in lieu of site control and commercial readiness will help deter speculative hybrid projects.
if a hybrid project has site control and commercial readiness satisfied with binding off-take/ load agreements, then they should not be subject to those deposits.

letters.desc: Buckeye supports a crediting mechanism tied to actual data center usage rather than automatic balloon payments, ensuring data centers receive credit for upfront costs only as they demonstrate sustained usage, which protects other wholesale customers from bearing stranded costs.
quotes: Crediting would provide the large data center with the opportunity to receive full credits for its upfront payments to the extent that it has sufficient usage over a sustained period of time, thereby protecting other wholesale customers from bearing stranded costs.

letters.org: California Department of Water Resources State Water Project
letters.desc: DWR calls for a crediting mechanism that conditions repayment on a significant portion of requested load showing up over a sustained period, distinguishing it from generator interconnection credits that are not tied to usage levels.
quotes: This assignment of costs should be paired with an appropriate crediting mechanism. This crediting mechanism might vary from region-to-region, but it must be designed to keep wholesale customers whole and disincentivize speculative load that will impose costs on wholesale customers.
Such a guaranteed crediting mechanism should not be adopted for large load interconnections because these credits are not tied to particular levels of usage.

letters.desc: CAISO supports standardized study deposits and readiness requirements, asking that any final rule allow transmission providers to align new large load procedures with those already accepted under Order No. 2023.
quotes: The CAISO supports this proposal, and recommends that if the Commission ultimately mandates specific reforms on this area, that any final rule enable transmission providers to align the large load processes with the processes transmission providers have established in complying with Order No. 2023.

letters.desc: The CPUC supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to protect ratepayers from stranded or mis-sized transmission assets. California is already developing similar mechanisms through its Rule 30 and CAISO proceedings.
quotes: The CPUC supports ratepayer protections and efforts to mitigate risks associated with stranded or mis-sized transmission assets.

letters.org: CHAMBER OF COMMERCE OF THE UNITED STATES
letters.desc: The Chamber asks that the fourth principle be strengthened with study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter duplicative and speculative requests and improve the accuracy of anticipated load growth.
quotes: The ANOPR's fourth principle should be strengthened to include study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties that enhance the veracity and transparency of the load growth currently anticipated across the power grid.

letters.desc: Crusoe backs sharply higher deposit fees (at least $100,000) and mandatory site control to block speculative queue entries. It also wants objective technical and financial criteria, not just qualitative curtailment pledges, so queue positions reflect real development intent.
quotes: Speculative interconnection requests are hindering AI deployment across the country.  Speculative requests will continue to delay interconnection for large scale projects and lead to uncertainty in real load demand.

Crusoe supports the comments of Google and OpenAI asking the Commission to impose heightened standards for interconnection requests, including significant increase in deposit fees and site control requirements to deter speculative requests.

The Commission should instead establish clear, objective criteria that require interconnection customers to demonstrate both technical capability and financial commitment beyond mere qualitative assurances of curtailment flexibility.
Such qualification standards can include site control requirements, minimum queue fees of $100,000 or greater, and tendering full security for transmission upgrades.

letters.desc: DPN supports standardized study deposits to deter speculative requests that flood utilities, but wants them non-trivial yet not excessive and credited back over the first contract year.
quotes: Study deposits would assist in solving the problem of entities flooding utilities with requests for load.
Given that data centers are not subject to paying these deposits now, these payments should be credited back over the first year of the contract.

letters.desc: Duke Energy supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative queue entries, consistent with its own existing retail practices.
quotes: standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties will help to deter speculative requests.

letters.desc: EDF supports adopting the LGIP's staged readiness deposits and withdrawal penalties for large load interconnection queues to deter speculative filings and give transmission providers timely, accurate information for studies.
quotes: Standardized provisions with deadlines, staged readiness deposits, and withdrawal penalties help deter speculative projects and provide transmission providers with the necessary and timely information to enable more accurate study of a new large load's impact on the transmission system.

letters.desc: EEI supports study deposits sized to both cover study costs and discourage speculative queue entries, drawing on the lesson from generator interconnection queues that became unmanageable when readiness requirements were weak.
quotes: EEI member companies agree that any large-load interconnection program or tariff adopted by the Commission must address speculative projects and provide a framework to allow transmission providers to more accurately forecast demand on their systems. With a large load interconnection, a study will need to be performed. Study deposits sufficient not only to cover the cost of the study but also to deter speculative study requests are appropriate.

Generator interconnection queues became unmanageable precisely because they permitted entry without strong readiness requirements which hindered transmission planning and delayed needed infrastructure.

letters.desc: ELCON supports readiness requirements, deposits, and penalties modeled on generator interconnection to remove speculative projects and improve load forecasting accuracy, but cautions that existing regional arrangements must not be rendered unworkable. Steep deposit levels risk disadvantaging capital-constrained industrial applicants relative to well-capitalized developers.
quotes: While ELCON agrees with principle four that the Commission should require implementation of readiness requirements, deposits, and penalties to large load interconnection requests similar to the generator interconnection process, these readiness requirements may already exist in many regions and the Commission should not take any action that would render these established and agreed upon requirements unworkable.

Requirements that are specifically targeted to remove speculative projects that will never be built (or projects that 'shop' multiple connection points) will effectively reduce the number of studies to be performed and provide a more accurate load forecast.

We caution the Commission to be aware that developers with massive amounts of capital can push other projects, that struggle to meet steep readiness obligations, further down the interconnection queue.

letters.desc: ECA endorses financial commitments, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties as tools to discipline load forecasts and deter speculative or duplicative interconnection requests.
quotes: study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties are critical components of the large load interconnection process. As the Secretary notes, these requirements and financial commitments are important to discipline load forecasts, avoid duplicative interconnection requests from the same large load customer for the same facility, and limit speculation by large load customers that drive inflated load forecasts.

letters.desc: ECA supports preserving all options for large customers to fund network upgrades with private capital rather than through ratepayer-funded rate base. ECA endorses open season models and opposes mandates that limit private investment pathways.
quotes: The Commission should, as a general matter, avoid taking options off the table for large customers to fund with private capital rather than ratepayer funds the new transmission and generation infrastructure needed to serve them.

Mandating that all transmission upgrades be funded by transmission providers in rate base with a return on investment, or that customers securitize network upgrades that transmission providers are funding through rate base, would lead to increased costs and less options to support speed to power without any demonstrable benefit to other customers.

ECA supports further examination of the potential for open season models to allow customers to express interest in funding new infrastructure or flexibly utilizing off-peak capacity to meet their needs.

letters.desc: ECA identifies upfront payments, long-term service commitments, minimum billing obligations, exit charges, and financial assurance requirements as among the most important consumer protection tools. These mechanisms, already common in retail large load tariffs, should be extended or mirrored at the federal wholesale level to reduce stranded cost risk.
quotes: upfront payments, long-term service commitments, minimum billing obligations, exit charges, and financial assurance requirements may be among the most important consumer protection tools in the large load context.

letters.desc: ENGIE endorses per-MW deposits of $5,000 to $10,000 and withdrawal penalties as reasonable financial commitments. It also calls for tariffs to publish clear timelines for deposit requirements and study schedules.
quotes: Financial requirements, including deposits of $5,000-$10,000 per megawatt of load are reasonable as are penalties for facilities that exit interconnection studies.

ENGIE also supports transparency and accountability in the interconnection process by requiring transmission providers to publish tariffs with clear and well understood timelines for deposit requirements.

letters.desc: Entergy agrees that steps to deter speculative loads from clogging interconnection queues are reasonable and should be part of any final rule.
quotes: we also agree that it is reasonable to take steps to deter speculative loads from delaying the interconnection of genuine projects.

letters.desc: Current deposit proposals cover only distribution facilities; ELPC recommends requiring deposits for all incremental costs regardless of how the utility classifies the facilities, to prevent ratepayers from absorbing stranded transmission investments if a large-load project withdraws.
quotes: the Commission should order ComEd to collect deposits for the incremental costs of Large Demand Project Applicants or Customers, regardless of whether those costs are deemed by ComEd to be transmission costs or distribution costs.

letters.desc: Eolian links up-front cost certainty to queue efficiency, arguing it is the single most powerful tool for reducing speculative withdrawals and restudies. It favors Transmission Security Commitments over facility-specific deposit or direct assignment regimes that replicate the uncertainty plaguing generator interconnection.
quotes: FERC could avoid repeating the problems that have plagued generator interconnection queues through an approach that provides greater up-front cost certainty to interconnection customers, which is the single most powerful tool for reducing speculative and duplicative requests, study complexity, and re-studies.

letters.desc: ETX supports modeling the new Load Interconnection Study Procedures on FERC's Form LGIP, including graduated and escalating deposits with formulaic refundability in early stages. It also recommends adding a permitting and community acceptance criterion as the most meaningful commercial readiness gate.
quotes: FERC's Form LGIP for generation resources is a reasonable pro-forma for graduated/escalating study deposits and readiness requirements for a new load study procedure ("Load Interconnection Study Procedures"), including formulaic mechanisms for refundability of deposits in the early stages of the process.
The additional and most potent commercial readiness criteria ETX recommends for consideration by the Commission is a Permitting and/or Public Acceptance qualification.

letters.desc: Exelon supports Transmission Security Agreements, which function as take-or-pay transmission revenue commitments, combined with expanded retail deposit requirements. This combination deters speculative requests and protects existing ratepayers without removing large loads from the shared transmission revenue base.
quotes: Overstated demand expectations can, and likely will, trigger costly system upgrades or new facility construction to serve that anticipated demand. If expected demand never materializes, infrastructure and capacity costs can end up borne by other customers.
These agreements are designed to ensure that a contribution to the transmission revenue requirement is made by large load customers commensurate with their requested end-use retail demand.
The design of the TSA is intended to weed out speculative customer behavior while protecting other customers in the event a large load project realizes less than its promised load.

letters.desc: Fervo supports readiness criteria that mirror generator standards, including site control and contracting milestones, to distinguish commercially viable projects and improve queue efficiency without imposing excessive financial barriers.
quotes: Fervo supports the Commission's focus on ensuring that large-load and hybrid interconnection customers demonstrate commercial readiness before entering and advancing through the interconnection queue. Fervo encourages the Commission to prioritize readiness criteria that mirror the maturity expectations already applied to large generator interconnection customers, including demonstrated site control or contracting milestones.

Applying a readiness framework to load and hybrid customers can help transmission providers distinguish commercially viable projects, improve queue efficiency, and reduce speculative requests without imposing unnecessary financial barriers.

letters.org: Georgia Power CompanyAlabama Power CompanyMississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: Southern Companies point to minimum bill requirements, longer contract terms, and termination provisions as the mechanism that ensures large loads pay their own way. These tools have not deterred data center development in the Southeast.
quotes: A combination of minimum bill requirements, termination provisions, and longer contract terms can help to ensure that data centers and other large load customers pay the full cost of serving them and avoid any risk that existing retail customers, particularly working families, seniors and small businesses, will be left to bear the costs.
large load customers acknowledge the demands they place on existing infrastructure and are willing to pay their share of generation and transmission costs in exchange for timely service.

letters.desc: The GPSC adopted minimum billing requirements and early termination fees for customers over 100 MW as a form of financial commitment, ensuring cost recovery without shifting costs to existing ratepayers.
quotes: the GPSC has acted in the past year to further solidify its regulatory mandate in response to the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads. In April 2025 the Commission approved changes to its rules and regulations requiring Georgia Power to ensure that new customers over 100 MW pay their cost of service through minimum billing requirements, long term contracts with sizable fees in the case of early termination, and other terms and conditions

letters.desc: Google supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for all new large loads. It advocates for its Capacity Commitment Framework, which requires long-term contracts, minimum demand charges, and upfront collateral to deter speculative interconnection requests and anchor load forecasts.
quotes: The Commission should craft procedures to expedite the transmission-level interconnection of new load and electrically proximate generation where a large load developer makes a financial commitment, via a power purchase agreement ('PPA') or a similar agreement, to bring online a new generating facility, uprate or expand an existing generating facility, retain a generating facility that would otherwise retire, or enable a resource that would otherwise be uneconomic to undergo fuel-switching.

All new loads interconnecting to the transmission system—whether paired with co-located or electrically proximate generation or not—should be subject to safeguards to protect other customers and ratepayers.

When public utilities create load forecasts for wholesale market administration and transmission planning, they should include large loads in the forecast only if the developer has made appropriate and verifiable financial commitments commensurate with their stage in the development process.

letters.desc: GridCARE recommends a load-interconnection study-fee framework that scales with load size and complexity and rewards demonstrated flexibility, analogous to the generator fee structure in Order No. 2023, to discourage speculative or inflated queue filings.
quotes: the Commission should establish a load-interconnection study-fee framework that scales with the size and complexity of the proposed load and reflects the level of operational flexibility demonstrated by the customer.

letters.desc: Heron asks the Commission to explore reduced study deposit requirements for facilities whose open, documented control behavior lowers the study burden on operators.
quotes: The Commission should also explore preferential queue treatment or reduced study deposit requirements for such facilities, recognizing that the study burden those facilities impose on operators is materially lower.

letters.desc: The IL OAG supports tailored deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties calibrated to prevent speculative filings. It cites the ComEd pipeline of 28,000 MW, exceeding ComEd's all-time peak, as evidence that the current queue is inflated with projects unlikely to be built.
quotes: Study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties must be designed to ensure that large loads and associated generation have the resources to proceed, are not speculative, and do not waste utility and other resources on projects that are not ready to implement.

letters.desc: The filer endorses the ANOPR's proposal for study deposits and readiness requirements, viewing them as a practical check on speculative and duplicative interconnection requests that inflate queue length and delay processing.
quotes: The Indicated PJM TOs agree with principle 4 of the ANOPR proposal to the extent that it requires reasonable study deposits and readiness requirements for large load interconnections. These measures will help ensure that large load customers are sufficiently invested in the load interconnection process, which will deter speculative or duplicative requests.

letters.desc: iMasons supports standardized deposits and withdrawal penalties only when they are proportionate to actual risks posed to transmission owners. It opposes revenue guarantee frameworks that require large financial commitments regardless of actual costs incurred, and opposes utility capacity clawbacks.
quotes: Deposits and penalties should be fashioned in a manner that mitigates risks and costs that large loads actually pose to transmission owners and other customers.

Requirements that are disproportionate to the risk and costs that large loads actually pose to transmission owners and other customers do not help protect consumers, and instead, overcompensate utilities and risk stifling the market for data centers in the United States.

the TSA construct, and any similar 'revenue guarantee' proposals that may be proposed by other transmission owners, would clearly run afoul of the Commission's cost causation principal, which requires 'that all approved rates reflect to some degree the costs actually caused by the customer [that] must pay them.'
the Commission should not permit utilities to 'claw back' capacity that has already been secured by a large load developer or hyperscale end-user.

letters.desc: IFP supports Principle 4's deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties as necessary to filter out speculative projects and give transmission providers more accurate demand forecasts.
quotes: Principle 4, which calls for standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties, is a necessary means of filtering out speculative projects, providing transmission providers with more useful information to more accurately forecast demand on their systems.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties sized to actual project and network upgrade costs. For hybrids, a single deposit based on the larger of the load or generation size prevents double-counting. Extraneous application data requirements like ramp rates, job counts, and water usage add no interconnection value and should be prohibited.
quotes: transmission owners too often require developers to post billions of dollars in security up front to interconnect hybrid facilities without any regard to the actual cost of interconnecting and serving data center load, in some instances requiring hybrid projects to securitize both the load and generation interconnection requests.

study deposits for large load and hybrid facilities should be based on the size of the request. For hybrid interconnection requests, there should be only one study deposit that is based on the greater of the generation size or load size, but not both.

Any commercial readiness or security required should be determined based on the amount of the network upgrades required to interconnect the load, consistent with the generator interconnection rules and the Commission's cost causation policy.

load serving entities often require detailed specifications for data center projects at the time of application including ramp rate schedules, planned total investment, number of jobs created, water usage, and local ordinance approvals, among other detailed information about planned facilities. This information is not often available to generation and data center developers at the outset of the interconnection process and bears no relevance to studying the interconnection

letters.desc: ISO-NE supports standardized deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties. It recommends adding non-financial readiness criteria such as site control, permits, and equipment orders to filter out speculative projects.
quotes: ISO-NE agrees with this principle.  In addition, non-financial readiness requirements, such as site control, permits, and equipment orders, should also be included to ensure that only requests for "first ready," viable, large load and hybrid facility projects enter the interconnection process.

letters.desc: The KCC identifies a gap in federal law: unlike its own LLPS tariff, nothing currently requires large loads to commit to paying for regional transmission projects before those projects are built. It views this as a necessary federal reform that can be addressed within the existing jurisdictional structure.
quotes: there is currently no mechanism under federal statutes or regulations that require projected loads to commit to pay for the regional projects ahead of building those projects

letters.desc: LPPC supports standardized deposits and withdrawal penalties for large load, but flags that IRS private-use rules on tax-exempt bonds cap public power contract terms at three years, which complicates enforcement and requires coordination with Treasury.
quotes: LPPC asks the Commission to clarify that the ANOPR's disclaimer reserving authority to states encompasses not only rates for direct retail sales but also the ability of Load Serving Entities ("LSEs") to assess the cost of new generation needed to serve large data centers at the outset of service, and to require contractual commitments of specified length to assure cost recovery.

Customer Agreements longer than three years are treated as "private use" under Treas. Reg. § 1.141-7(f)(3), which caps contract terms at three years. Because tax exempt bonds are subject to private business use limits on a system wide and long-term basis, a single large customer contract that fails the current three year test can cause outstanding tax exempt bonds to become taxable private activity bonds.

letters.desc: LPPC describes financial assurance practices, including required collateral or creditworthiness demonstrations before construction and upfront funding commitments, as standard tools its members use to ensure large loads can cover their costs.
quotes: LPPC member utilities are employing a variety of customer-protective mechanisms, including dedicated substations, upfront infrastructure funding requirements, take-or-pay provisions, minimum billing demand charges, exit fees, and bring-your-own-power arrangements, to ensure large load growth does not burden existing ratepayers.
Requires the customer to post collateral or demonstrate creditworthiness prior to construction.

letters.desc: LS Power supports standardized deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties built on the existing generation interconnection pro-forma, with added provisions for cost and schedule accountability drawn from competitive Designated Entity Agreements.
quotes: The existing generation interconnection frameworks should be used and improved upon to establish standardized pro-forma terms for large load interconnections.

letters.desc: Maryland supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties mirroring those for generators. Such requirements deter speculative projects and improve demand forecasting accuracy for transmission planning.
quotes: like generating facilities, load and hybrid facilities should be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties
Imposing financial and readiness requirements is important to limit the inclusion of speculative projects that are unlikely to materialize

letters.org: Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General
letters.desc: The State Entities call for financial protections that shield ratepayers if large load customers fail to materialize, abandon projects, or exit the system early, preventing stranded transmission costs from being socialized onto existing customers.
quotes: The Commission's rulemaking should also include protections that shield ratepayers from cost risk associated with large load customers that fail to materialize, abandon interconnecting projects, or prematurely exit the transmission system.

letters.desc: The filer endorses requiring data centres to pay upfront fees before securing a queue position, citing AEP Ohio's tariff as evidence that such requirements reduce speculative applications and protect ratepayers from stranded upgrade costs.
quotes: Speculative requests for connections are either not backed by a finalised project but serve as a way to hold a place in queue as the project is developed, or an existing project that applies for connections in multiple locations with the intent of building in only the one that gives them the lowest cost.
Requiring data centres to bear upfront costs could help minimise speculative data centre connection requests.

letters.desc: Microsoft supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to add regulatory certainty, deter speculation, and improve transparency. It wants processes that clearly state study requirements, financial commitments, timelines, and the duties of both utility and customer.
quotes: Microsoft supports standardizing study requirements to provide greater regulatory certainty, deter speculation, and enhance transparency so businesses can plan with more predictability.
Interconnection processes should clearly articulate study requirements, financial commitments, timelines, and responsibilities of the utility and the customer.

letters.desc: Missouri PSC supports strong financial requirements to deter speculative projects and protect customers from stranded costs, including for co-located generation that may become unnecessary as technology evolves.
quotes: Other customers should not bear the costs of co-located generation that becomes unnecessary if, for example, data centers become more efficient over time.
The final rule should adopt strong requirements to deter speculative projects, fairly allocate costs and enhance transparency.

letters.org: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
letters.desc: NARUC cites state-approved collateral, deposit, and sliding-scale fee structures, such as Virginia's collateral requirements and Illinois's study deposits, as effective tools that discourage speculative requests and protect ratepayers from stranded costs.
quotes: this new large load tariff requires a minimum contract term of 14 years, a maximum ramp period of four years, minimum collateral requirements, and minimum demand charges based on contracted capacity.  All these protections will ensure that costs are not shifted to non-large load customers.

This sliding-scale approach provides appropriate incentives for customers to submit realistic and supportable demand forecasts and helps mitigate the risk of speculative or inflated requests that could lead to inefficient planning or unnecessary system investment.

letters.org: National Association of State Utility Consumer Advocates
letters.desc: Strong readiness and financial requirements are needed to deter speculative large-load interconnection requests that distort transmission planning and increase costs for consumers.
quotes: strong readiness and financial requirements to deter speculative large-load interconnection requests that can distort transmission planning and increase costs for consumers

letters.org: Office of the Ohio Consumers' Counsel
letters.desc: OCC supports non-refundable, project-size-scaled study deposits and withdrawal penalties to discourage speculative queue entries, which distort demand forecasts and trigger premature network upgrades recovered from consumers.
quotes: speculative filings- particularly by unconfirmed data center and industrial developers- have contributed to inaccurate demand forecasts and queue congestion, which can lead to unnecessary or premature network upgrades later recovered from consumers.
OCC also supports scaling study deposits and readiness milestones to project size, with non-refundable deposits and withdrawal penalties to discourage speculative queue participation.

letters.desc: Ohio FEA endorses standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for data centers across the country to filter speculative loads, free up utility resources, and improve forecasting. AEP Ohio's experience shows deposits reduced projected data center load from over 30,000 MW to under 15,000 MW.
quotes: the Ohio FEA supports the use of standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for data center loads across the country

Such financial obligations and milestones are necessary to separate legitimate loads that are ready for interconnection service from loads that are speculative, redundant, or unlikely to move forward.

This frees up limited utility resources to be spent on projects that are truly shovel-ready. It also informs critical utility load forecasting and planning processes, helping to prevent misallocation of resources or overinvestment in the system.

To illustrate, last year, AEP Ohio projected over 30,000 MW of new data center load interconnections. However, once its data center tariff was in place and a one-time fee was established to conduct a formal study, that number was cut by more than half.

letters.desc: ODEC generally supports standardized study deposits and readiness requirements for large loads but says they require a dedicated large-load queue with load forecasts and operating protocols to be administered effectively.
quotes: ODEC generally supports this principle but strongly recommends creating a large load queue, along with load forecasts and operating protocols, to help administer these requirements.

letters.desc: OpenAI wants reduced withdrawal penalties for ready projects with valid end-user agreements that withdraw for reasons beyond their control, while keeping full penalties for speculative loads without offtake agreements.
quotes: Forlargeloadprojectsthatmeetthereadinesscriteriaandhavesecuredvalidenduser agreements but subsequently withdraw for reasonsbeyondtheircontrol,withdrawalpenalties shouldbereduced.
Speculativeloadsthatwithdrawwithoutenduserofftakeagreementsshould remain subject to full withdrawal penalties.

letters.desc: OPSI supports measures to ensure large loads bear their fair share of transmission costs and to deter harmful speculation in the interconnection queue.
quotes: It is imperative that large loads looking to interconnect bear their fair share of transmission costs and that the Commission deter harmful speculation as these loads seek to interconnect.

letters.desc: PG&E supports standardized deposits and readiness requirements as an effective filter against speculative interconnection requests, while asking for some regional flexibility on amounts and specifics.
quotes: PG&E supports this proposal as an effective way to address speculative projects and to provide transmission providers with useful information.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers support a centrally managed interconnection queue with standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects and improve demand forecasting accuracy.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates support establishing a large load and hybrid interconnection queue that is centrally managed by the same entity that manages/administers resource adequacy processes, like PJM. This queue should have standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects and provide transmission providers and RTOs with useful information to forecast demand on their systems accurately.

letters.desc: Shell Energy calls study deposits and readiness criteria the single most important ANOPR principle. Deposits tied to transparency reporting will improve load forecast credibility, deter speculative applications, and allow capacity markets to reflect realistic demand without waiting for longer-running reforms.
quotes: First and highest priority should be for improving accuracy of load projections used in current competitive markets.
Shell Energy views this as the most important principle proposed in the ANOPR. This reform, with proper transparency reporting, significantly improves the credibility of the load forecasts.

At the time of entry into load queue, Shell Energy supports study deposits, readiness requirements including application fees, and withdrawal penalties for load interconnection requests similar to existing generator interconnections studies and application fees.
Including large loads that pay study deposits and meet established readiness criteria in capacity market demand curves can be executed efficiently relative to other reforms.

Existing loads under study, and ongoing stakeholder processes to develop expedited large load processes should prioritize how to improve transparency to the market about the volume of load under study and readiness status of the load.

letters.desc: SMA recommends differentiated and proportionate study deposits for proven grid-supportive technology providers, specifically a 15 percent reduction in initial deposits for applicants with a demonstrated track record. This would lower market entry barriers without enabling speculative projects.
quotes: SMA recommends that FERC consider differentiated and proportionate study deposits and readiness requirements for grid-supportive technology providers.
SMA suggests reducing initial deposit requirements by approximately 15 percent for applicants with a proven track record of delivering grid-supportive performance.

letters.desc: SEIA supports standard study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to screen out speculative requests. However, SEIA conditions this support on equal transparency from transmission providers about how they will establish load projections.
quotes: SEIA generally supports instituting standard study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for the interconnection of large loads, co-located generation and BYOG.
increased site control requirements must also come with increased transparency in how the transmission providers will establish load projections.

letters.org: Southern Company Services, Inc.Alabama Power CompanyGeorgia Power Company ,Mississippi Power Company ,
letters.desc: Southern Companies cite collateral requirements and long-term contractual commitments among the tools that protect existing customers from large-load risk.
quotes: Georgia Power Company has implemented several mechanisms aimed to protect existing customers, including minimum bill obligations for large loads, long-term contractual commitments, collateral requirements, termination protection, and regulatory review and accountability for customer-specific arrangements.

letters.org: Southern Environmental Law CenterAppalachian VoicesNorth Carolina Sustainable Energy Association ,South Carolina Coastal Conservation League ,Southern Alliance for Clean Energy ,
letters.desc: The filers urge the Commission to adopt study deposits, readiness deposits, and withdrawal penalties modeled on Order No. 2023, and to set them higher for large loads than for generators because large loads are sophisticated and less sensitive to price signals. Site control requirements should also be required before queue entry.
quotes: the lack of uniform conditions placed on large load interconnections to the transmission system fails to limit speculative interconnection requests, which could lead to overbuilding, a heightened risk of stranded investment, and unjust and unreasonable rates borne by transmission customers.
The Commission should implement study deposits, readiness deposits, and withdrawal penalties in any standardized large load interconnection procedures.
the Commission should require large loads to pay higher study deposits and withdrawal penalties than those applicable to generator interconnections.

letters.org: Southern Environmental Law CenterNorth Carolina Sustainable Energy AssociationAppalachian Voices ,Coastal Conservation League ,Southern Alliance for Clean Energy ,
letters.desc: The filers support requiring large loads to commit financially at the interconnection stage, earlier than retail service obligations typically attach. They argue this layered commitment approach is necessary given the enormous cost and price insensitivity of large load interconnections.
quotes: A large load interconnection process could require large loads to commit to an interconnection request earlier than when a retail service obligation would otherwise attach.

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The group endorses requiring sufficient upfront payments and penalties on large loads and generators seeking expedited interconnection to prevent speculative or duplicative projects from clogging the queue.
quotes: Imposing sufficient upfront payments and penalties on new large loads and generators to prevent speculative or duplicative projects from seeking expedited interconnection procedures, while mitigating the risk of inappropriate cost shifts or stranded costs

letters.org: Southwest Power Pool Transmission Owner Group
letters.desc: The SPP TO Group supports SPP's tiered fees and withdrawal penalties under HILL and CPP as sufficient to deter speculation and asks FERC not to override them with a new standard. The group is agnostic about the specific amounts required in other regions.
quotes: The HILL reform imposes a $10,000 non-refundable application fee, a $100,000 deposit to perform an HDPS study, a $200,000 fee for an EMT analysis if necessary, and increased deposits for requests to study and interconnect HILLs and HILLGAs.

The withdrawal penalty framework SPP has embraced satisfies Principle 4, and the Commission should not impose a new rule that interferes with what SPP and its stakeholders have accomplished.  The SPP TO Group remains agnostic as to the appropriate size of withdrawal penalties in other regions so long as they accomplish the ANOPR's intent to deter speculative projects.

letters.desc: SPP supports requiring meaningful study deposits and application fees so that only serious interconnection applicants enter the queue. SPP already applies this approach to its HILL and HILLGA processes.
quotes: SPP believes that any final rule related to the interconnection of large loads and supporting generation should include a level of financial commitment that ensures that SPP, and other transmission providers, are only studying those projects that fully intend to interconnect to their transmission system.

letters.desc: Switch supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to filter out speculative projects. The company argues the Commission should condition interconnection priority on demonstrated site control, committed customers, permits, executed service agreements, and project financing.
quotes: If the Commission goes forward with the proposed ANOPR, it should focus on expediting interconnection of proven large load projects with demonstrated site control, committed customers, applicable permits, executed service agreements and/or project financing.

This approach is consistent with the fourth principle for reform in the proposed ANOPR about standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, withdrawal penalties and other commitments and financial penalties to deter speculative projects.
Any rules adopted by the Commission should prioritize projects that are ready for interconnection and reduce the incentives for speculative, non-viable projects.

letters.desc: Tesla backs study deposits and withdrawal penalties for large loads but wants the deposits credited back, possibly through transmission credits, since prior load requests were not subject to such mechanisms.
quotes: Tesla is generally supportive of concepts that limit duplicative load interconnection requests; however, we believe that requirements should be instituted for large loads presumed to be data centers or crypto mining centers.
a system should be established to provide credit back for study deposits, but perhaps through transmission credits.

letters.desc: Cost assignments, including deposits, should reflect the costs a load actually imposes on the system, giving credit for benefits such as peak avoidance.
quotes: Cost allocation should reflect the principle that customers pay the costs they impose on the system, minus any benefits they provide.

letters.desc: TAPS supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for large load interconnections, mirroring reforms adopted for generator queues in Order 2023 to reduce speculative withdrawals and restudies.
quotes: standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties would be beneficial in the context of Qualifying Large Load interconnections. As in the context of generator interconnections, these kinds of requirements are needed to deter speculative requests that may begin the study process but then withdraw, causing delays and restudies.

letters.org: Utility Intervention Unit, New York State Department of Stat
letters.desc: The UIU supports requiring large loads and hybrid facilities to post the same study deposits, meet readiness milestones, and face withdrawal penalties as generators, deterring speculative queue entries.
quotes: UIU supports the ANOPR proposal to require that generating facilities, load and hybrid facilities be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties.

letters.desc: Verrus argues that collateral should match actual stranded-cost exposure during the construction window, mirroring the generator interconnection model. Blanket deposits tied to theoretical upgrade costs exclude less-capitalized innovative entrants without providing proportionate ratepayer protection.
quotes: Credit assurance should protect ratepayers from stranded-cost risk—not serve as a barrier to participation. Today, many utilities require deposits equal to multiple years of transmission revenue or theoretical upgrade costs regardless of a project's actual risk profile or contribution to bulk system upgrades. Such rules privilege only the largest incumbents and exclude technically capable but less capitalized entrants.

Credit requirements should scale with the actual infrastructure spend required to interconnect the large load. As in the generator interconnection process, credit requirements should secure actual interconnection costs, but only during the period of construction when ratepayers are exposed to those costs.

letters.desc: The VSCC supports standardized study deposits and readiness requirements but argues these should be set by FERC as minimum standards and implemented by states, not run through RTO tariffs. Nearly half of states including Virginia are already developing such standards.
quotes: Develop a set of Commission-mandated minimum standards for large load interconnections, such as study deposits, site control requirements, and similar criteria while allowing transmission owners, and not the RTOs, who already face long delays and inefficiencies in their existing generation queues, to continue to manage large load interconnection queues with direct oversight of their state regulatory commissions.

The ANOPR also suggests that "load and hybrid facilities should be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties." Like almost half of the states, the VSCC is currently considering new large load tariffs and addressing just those issues.

letters.desc: The VSCC supports commercial readiness requirements, including credit and collateral obligations, but specifies they must balance deterring speculative projects against discouraging real investment.
quotes: Commercial readiness payments, such as credit and collateral obligations, should be designed to appropriately balance real, customer-specific risk without deterring investment.

letters.desc: Vistra supports standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to screen out speculative projects and protect ratepayers from costs attributable to data centers that never get built.
quotes: the current lack of standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties increases the prevalence of speculative projects and the related risk that ratepayers will be saddled with costs incurred due to projects that never materialize.

letters.desc: Vistra supports participant funding as the preferred cost allocation model, where large loads pay 100% of incremental network upgrade costs they cause. It also endorses study deposits and withdrawal penalties to screen out speculative requests and provide cost certainty for commercial agreements.
quotes: Cost causation principles require that the parties to such an arrangement fund any necessary network upgrades, and the transmission service that facilitates these arrangements be determined by actual use of the transmission system based on their net load.

The third option, to contrast, creates a significant risk of cost shifts to other customers if a large load customer fails to materialize, consumes less energy than intended, or ceases operation sooner than anticipated.

Participant funding also furthers speed to power by providing cost certainty that can be built into a large load customer's commercial negotiations, whereas a crediting approach could entail more uncertainty and necessitate a risk premium in commercial arrangements.
a standardized process could include study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects that are unlikely to materialize.

letters.desc: Buckeye supports study deposits and withdrawal penalties as tools to reduce speculative queue entries but is explicit that these measures do not address stranded cost risks that arise after transmission is built and large loads fail to sustain expected demand.
quotes: Buckeye supports requirements to deter speculative projects, such as standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties.

Although these requirements may prevent speculative projects from entering the study process, they do not address the major stranded cost concerns with data centers that complete the study process, cause massive transmission upgrades, but then do not have the expected level of demand over a sustained period.

letters.desc: Geronimo Power contends that study deposits and withdrawal penalties, while useful, will not deter speculative submissions by well-capitalized data center developers and must be supplemented by substantive viability criteria such as a binding capacity commitment.
quotes: There is no reason to believe that exclusively relying on study deposits, withdrawal penalties, or other financial indications of readiness will be sufficient to deter the submission of requests by speculative or immature projects.

The Commission can avoid repeating the mistakes that led to unmanageable generator interconnection queues by requiring that large loads demonstrate that their load is supported by a binding commitment of capacity sufficient to serve a significant proportion of their needs given the specified operational characteristics of the load.

letters.desc: The Maryland PSC shares concern about speculative projects but opposes imposing deposit and penalty requirements directly on retail load customers. It recommends that anti-speculation obligations fall on load-serving entities, which are under FERC's wholesale jurisdiction.
quotes: Principle 4, as it purports to apply to load and hybrid facilities with load greater than 20 MW, would impose requirements and penalties directly on large load customers, which are retail customers currently subject to retail tariffs regardless of where they interconnect. This raises potential jurisdictional conflicts with state-level requirements placed on end-use customers via state-specific retail tariffs.

the Commission should focus on solutions that would preclude speculation and hold the wholesale intermediary (over which FERC has jurisdiction) accountable for the accuracy of its load projections and supplying that load

letters.desc: MISO acknowledges that if a load queue were created, deposits and withdrawal penalties would be needed to deter speculative entries, consistent with what Order No. 2023 imposed on generators. However, MISO prefers its existing pre-screening approach over formal queue discipline.
quotes: only about 13% of the total capacity entering interconnection queues nationwide ultimately achieves commercial operation.  Withdrawals of speculative interconnection requests frequently require restudies, particularly for later-stage withdrawals, which in turn could delay completion of studies and ultimately delay bringing viable generation proposals online.

letters.desc: The filer acknowledges that speculative load is a real problem but notes many MISO transmission owners already require financial commitments from load customers. Federal deposit requirements risk duplicating or conflicting with these existing state and tariff mechanisms.
quotes: Speculative load requests do exist, but to deter speculative load requests, many transmission owners and LSEs already require financial commitments from load customers to develop the transmission facilities needed to serve new large loads.

letters.desc: The Market Monitor acknowledges deposit requirements as a tool to screen out speculative projects but argues that an expedited bring-your-own-generation option is a stronger and more targeted incentive.
quotes: The best incentive to bring only real projects is to provide an expedited option to bring your own new generation. This incentive would be much stronger and more effective and more focused on a real solution than requiring deposits.

letters.desc: Agrees that standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties are needed, but these solutions are best addressed at the local level through RTOs and state commissions, not through uniform federal rules applied to all loads in all areas.
quotes: the NPRB agrees with the Secretary of Energy that standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties are needed when dealing with the interconnection of proposed large loads, the NPRB believes these solutions are best addressed at the local level, not through a standardized set of rules for all types of loads in all areas of the country.

letters.desc: Terraflux agrees that deterrence mechanisms are appropriate but opposes mirroring Order 2023 financial amounts. It argues those amounts already concentrate queue access among large developers, and urges FERC to find alternative deterrence tools that do not act as entry and exit taxes.
quotes: FERC should not set load interconnection requirements to exactly mirror those the amounts established in Order No. 2023. The financial and commercial requirements set in the generator interconnection reform process, although successful in lowering the number of generation interconnection requests to be studied, have dissuaded inventive but less-resourced generation interconnection customers from being studied in the queues.
The reformed generation procedures favor large balance sheet and often less-nimble interconnection customers to crowd-out and morph generator interconnection queues into oligopolies.

FERC should consider alternative ways to deter load interconnection requests which have no intention of being built, rather than imposing significant entry taxes and exit taxes for load interconnection customers to be studied by the grid operator.

letters.desc: Tract accepts standardized deposits and financial security in principle but insists they be sized to actual incremental costs, not set as revenue guarantees for utilities. Security should be posted at project milestones rather than as an upfront lump sum, and agreements must be assignable to creditworthy third parties.
quotes: Tract agrees with adopting standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties, provided that they are consistent with the Commission's cost-causation principles.

Adopting deposits or penalties that are not sized to reflect a project's impact on the system will unnecessarily and economically deter data center development, threatening the ability to achieve the Administration's dual goals of energy dominance and winning the AI race.

The Commission should establish a standardized methodology, whether by requiring fixed deposit amounts based on load size, by kWh, or through another metric, whereby customers can reasonably calculate anticipated charges and plan their investments accordingly.

Tract appreciates the need to provide financial security for load interconnection requests, but believes financial security requirements should be clear, predictable, in line with cost-causation, and tied to project progress.

Consistent with the Commission's cost-causation principles, financial security should only be required for actual incremental costs caused by the large load customer, and should not provide a windfall to transmission providers in the event of default.

Tract recommends the Commission require large load interconnection customers to only post financial security as they approach key project milestones (i.e., to support detailed design, permitting and right-of-way acquisition, procurement, pad acceptance, construction and energization), rather than up front as a lump sum because this places an unnecessary financial burden on the large load interconnection customer and creates incremental impediments to development.
The Commission should require that large load interconnection agreements and any related financial security agreements be assignable to creditworthy third parties.

letters.desc: The Alliance opposes applying Order No. 2023's uniform study deposit and withdrawal penalty requirements to Tribal developers. It argues these requirements were designed to deter speculation by private actors and create a disparate burden on sovereign governments with distinct financing constraints. It calls for alternative commercial readiness criteria for Tribal entities.
quotes: Tribal Nations are sovereign entities, not similarly situated to other generation developers, and therefore should not be subject to the same commercial readiness and withdrawal penalty requirements of Order No. 2023, which were designed to deter speculative interconnection requests.

If left unmodified, the ANOPR's proposal to apply uniform study deposit and penalty requirements to large-load interconnections would perpetuate systemic inequities and further restrict Tribal participation in the energy transition.

We urge the Commission to clarify that these financial prerequisites will not be used to determine or influence queue position or expedited processing, as doing so would have a disparate impact on Tribally owned projects.

letters.desc: GridStor opposes applying large-load queuing and deposit requirements to ESRs, noting that ESRs already participate in generator interconnection queues with required deposits and readiness requirements, making added requirements onerously duplicative.
quotes: For example, it would be inappropriate and onerously duplicative to apply large loads queuing requirements as discussed in the ANOPR to apply to ESRs. Today, ESRs already participate in generator interconnection queuing processes with required deposits and readiness requirements, and ESRs execute interconnection agreements in a well-understood manner.

letters.desc: The filer opposes the ANOPR's suggestion of 100% participant funding, arguing it relies on embedded-cost methodologies that ignore marginal cost impacts and misalign incentives for large elastic loads.
quotes: The ANOPR's suggestion of 100% participant funding for upgrades relies on flawed embedded-cost methodologies that ignore marginal impacts.

letters.desc: The PA PUC identifies standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties for load facilities as one of the ANOPR reforms that collectively raise major-questions doctrine concerns without clear Congressional authorization.
quotes: The recommendations that (1) load and hybrid facilities be studied together with generating facilities for efficient siting and be subject to standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties; (2) hybrid facilities be studied based on the amount of injection and/or withdrawal rights requested to provide incentives for co-location with new generation facilities; (3) any hybrid interconnection install the system protection facilities necessary to prevent unauthorized injections or withdrawals that exceed the respective rights; (4) financial penalties for load facilities and hybrid facilities; (5) expedited consideration of interconnection studies of large loads and hybrid facilities that agree to be curtailable and dispatchable; and (6) that load and hybrid facilities should be responsible for 100% of the network upgrades that are assigned through the interconnection studies all have widespread economic and political ramifications.

letters.desc: APS seeks clarity on utility backup obligations when large loads co-locate with generators.
quotes: Is the utility expected to back up all, some, or none of the load for a large load that is co-locating with a generator?

letters.desc: PJM identifies open questions about how to set just-and-reasonable rates for study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties, including whether to follow state-law analogues and how to allocate collected funds.
quotes: what are just and reasonable rates for any standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties?  Would the federal load interconnection process and rate levels look to state law analogues where such constructs have already been developed?  Will such rates be postage stamp rates or connected to the scope and scale of the proposed load interconnection?
